Good morning, and happy Friday. **Andrew** here. You may have seen one of
**Donald Trump 's** lame-duck nominees roundly embarrass himself this week.
No, not [that one](https://x.com/CBSNews/status/2123454899790778818). Not
[that one](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2123112738314502550). I mean
_[that](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2123119253234806811)_[
one](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2123119253234806811).

**James Sullivan** , who can't remember what the 22nd Amendment does, could
soon have a lifetime gig in the federal judiciary. Unreported until now:
Sullivan's wife is a lawyer for **Elon Musk** , who has endless business in
the same district. Is any of that good?

In today's **' First Draft,'** we shine a light on Musk's latest gift from
Trump. Plus, New York Mayor **Zohran Mamdani** is determined to solve a
problem that has vexed the city for years: how to close the awful Rikers
Island jail.

And **Chris Van Hollen** has a new and 'moderate' senator backing his bid for
majority leader. Let's read on.

## **' Uphold the Rule of Law'? REALLY??**

Sullivan at his Senate Judiciary confirmation hearing on Nov. 18, 2026. Photo
via Senate Judiciary Committee._

Voters furiously rejected Donald Trump earlier this month, delivering
Democrats a series of wins in states they rarely compete in and a 56-seat
majority in the Senate.

Following their historic shellacking, Trump and Republicans are trying to ram
through as many embarrassing and
[shamelessly](https://x.com/CBSNews/status/2123454899790778818)
[MAGA](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2123112738314502550) nominees as they can,
before Democrats take power in January and presumably put a stop to it.

James Sullivan, one of Trump's nominees for a lifetime judicial appointment,
certainly fits the bill. Sullivan, a Texas Supreme Court justice who lost his
reelection, [claimed](https://x.com/JudgeSullyTX/status/2116170508412858709)
during his 2026 campaign that he would **" defend our Constitution and uphold
the rule of law."**

Yet, he made headlines at his confirmation hearing Wednesday for being [unable
to recall](https://people.com/trump-nominated-judge-refuses-to-say-he-cant-
run-for-third-term-12263450) what the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution does
- it bars the president from serving more than two terms - before refusing to
admit it means that Trump can't run for president again.

But Sullivan's extreme deference to Trump isn't the only concerning thing
about his nomination: He could also be Elon Musk's ace in the hole.

In a
[disclosure](https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/sullivan_sjq1.pdf)
to the Senate Judiciary Committee, Sullivan noted, **" My wife is a partner at
the law firm of Stone Hilton PLLC"** - which just so happens to be Musk's go-
to law firm. If confirmed, Sullivan would be a federal judge in the Western
District of Texas, which covers the Austin area, where the world's richest man
and some of his business interests are based.

Sullivan's wife, Alithea, [has
represented](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.txwd.1178532/gov.uscourts.txwd.1178532.12.0.pdf)
Musk and the board of his car company Tesla in the same district. She's also
[represented](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.txnd.383454/gov.uscourts.txnd.383454.170.0.pdf)
Musk's social media company, Twitter, in its ongoing lawsuit against Media
Matters - a case very obviously [meant](https://www.wired.com/story/x-elon-
musk-media-matters-lawsuit/) to chill the watchdog organization's journalism.
